docs.abstract: Figma, which makes a design platform, was on the verge of a big payday before regulators quashed the sale. On Thursday, it went public, with its stock ending the day up 250 percent.

byline.original: By Natallie Rocha and Michael J. de la Merced

headline.main: This Start-Up’s $20 Billion Sale Died. It Came Fighting Back.
headline.print_headline: The Revival Of a Start-Up Once Dead

multimedia.caption: Figma’s co-founder and chief executive, Dylan Field, with a hand on his right shoulder, before ringing the bell at the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday.
multimedia.credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
